scenes.heading: Hydrocarbons and fuels
scenes.sub: What's really in petrol, diesel and barbecue gas?
scenes.say: Petrol, diesel, barbecue gas and the gas in your stove are all made mostly of hydrocarbons. Welcome to organic chemistry, the chemistry of carbon compounds.

scenes.heading: Alkanes vs alkenes
scenes.say: A hydrocarbon contains only carbon and hydrogen. Alkanes have only single bonds, so they're saturated. Alkenes have one carbon-carbon double bond, so they're unsaturated and more reactive. An alkene quickly turns orange-brown bromine water colourless.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A Lego train that grows one carriage at a time
scenes.science: Each alkane is one CH₂ longer than the last
scenes.breaks: Lego carriages are identical, but end carbons carry CH₃ and middle ones CH₂, and real chains can branch.
scenes.say: Picture a Lego train that grows one carriage at a time. Each member of a homologous series is one C H two longer than the last. The prefix tells you how many carbon carriages there are, and the suffix tells you the family.
scenes.caption: Picture a Lego train that grows one carriage at a time. Each member of a homologous series is one CH₂ longer than the last. The prefix tells you how many carbon carriages there are, and the suffix tells you the family.

scenes.heading: Name that alkane
scenes.question: Write the molecular formula of the alkane with 5 carbons, and name it.
scenes.say: Remember: Monkeys Eat Peanut Butter, for meth, eth, prop and but, one to four carbons. For an alkane with five carbons, double the carbons and add two: twelve hydrogens. So it's C five H twelve. Pent plus ane gives pentane.
scenes.caption: Remember: Monkeys Eat Peanut Butter, for meth, eth, prop and but, 1 to 4 carbons. For an alkane with 5 carbons, double the carbons and add two: 12 hydrogens. So it's C₅H₁₂. Pent + ane gives pentane.

scenes.heading: Fractional distillation
steps: Vapour enters the bottom of the column
Each fraction condenses at its level
Small at the top, big at the bottom
scenes.say: Crude oil is a mixture, so it's separated by fractional distillation. It's heated into vapour, which rises up a column that's hot at the bottom and cool at the top. Each fraction condenses at its own level. Little ones fly high, big ones stay low.

scenes.heading: Complete combustion
scenes.say: When a fuel burns in plenty of oxygen, that's complete combustion. Methane plus two oxygen gives carbon dioxide plus two water. It's exothermic, so it releases heat. Balance these in C, H, O order: carbon first, then hydrogen, then oxygen last.

scenes.heading: Not enough air
scenes.everyday: A barbecue with blocked vents burns yellow and sooty
scenes.science: Limited oxygen gives carbon monoxide and soot
scenes.breaks: Flame colour is a clue, not a test: carbon monoxide has no colour or smell.
scenes.say: Block a barbecue's air vents and the flame turns yellow and sooty. That's incomplete combustion. With limited oxygen you get poisonous carbon monoxide and soot, and less energy. Carbon monoxide has no colour or smell, which is why gas heaters need ventilation.

Quick recap. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen. Alkanes are saturated, alkenes have a double bond. Crude oil is separated by boiling point. Complete combustion gives carbon dioxide and water. Now try the practice questions!
